_README: The year-ahead panel, as data instead of code. One object per condition. price_row_id points at a row that is already in prices.json, so no figure lives here and nothing new is asserted; the panel renders whatever that row says, with that row's year, population and coverage statement. A condition with price_row_id null renders the absence and sends the person to /gap so the gap is COUNTED rather than filled. Adding a condition is one object, but only after its figure exists as a verified row in prices.json. Since 2026-09-30 every entry also carries published_figures (figures about the condition that are not a year for one person: a count, a per-case cost, a national cost), each with two sources and the exact sentence from each, and example_journey, a sentence the /conditions page runs through the same reader. The shape of an entry is data/conditions.schema.json.
_the_distinction_that_must_stay_on_the_f: These figures are not the same KIND of number and must never be ranked against each other as if they were. An EXCESS figure is what a person spends OVER a comparable person who does not have the condition: the care the condition added. A CONDITION-ATTRIBUTED figure is what was spent on treating that condition, and it excludes everything else the person spent. figure_kind carries which one it is, and the panel prints it.

differs_from_journey: Different people: the study averages 613 reported cases, at least two of which cost over $100,000; the example is one sentence and the care it names.

Different prices: the study priced each billing code at what private insurers reimbursed, or at the Medicare fee schedule for people without private insurance; the tool prices every line at the national Medicare-allowed amount.
Different scope: the study counts every Lyme-related billing code a clinician sent, from a month before onset to the last monthly survey; the tool counts only the lines a person names.
A mean is pulled up by a few very expensive cases. The median, the middle case, is the closer yardstick for one ordinary journey, and it is printed beside the mean.

_icd10cm_source.what: Every ICD-10-CM code below was re-read in the code-description file CDC/NCHS publishes for the fiscal year, not typed from memory. The browser a clinician would use is the same data: https://icd10cmtool.cdc.gov/ (NCHS ICD-10-CM Web Application, multi-year edition).
_icd10cm_source.field_read: icd10cm-order-<FY>.txt, columns: order number, code, 1 if the code may be submitted on a claim / 0 if it is a category heading, short description, long description. The long description is what we print.
_icd10cm_source.why_two_years: The FY2027 code set takes effect on 1 October 2026. Every code here is present, billable-or-heading identical, and titled identically in both files, so nothing on this page changes when the code set turns over.
_icd10cm_source.first_effective_method: A first-effective date is asserted only where the code is ABSENT from an earlier year file and PRESENT in the year claimed. The earlier files read are FY2021 (icd10cm-codes-order-Jan-2021.zip, sha256 dffa100f5bc7e588cca63257c0da0668094b31ba9812283eba893d082d2e909f), FY2022 (2022/Code Descriptions zip.zip, sha256 bab2b3b041cf4b999f8380f3198c1dd6ca404ba7d5513ec60efc813a97f7c214) and FY2023 (icd10-Order-CodeFiles2023.zip, sha256 a7bfd4511dc154bff96fe0ced5fcd633bd26f997ccd6ae386f5c24595e1789b5). Where a code predates every file we read, we say that instead of inventing a date.

_no_code_is_not_an_oversight: Some rows here carry no ICD-10-CM code on purpose, and the count is printed from the data rather than written into the prose. AHRQ MEPS prices a CLINICAL CATEGORY ("adults treated for heart disease", "adults treated for diabetes"), which spans dozens of codes; picking one code to stand for it would misdescribe the population the figure came from. And there is no code for not yet having a diagnosis. A blank we can explain beats a code we cannot defend.
_sex_note_rule: Each condition carries what a federal source we opened and read says about sex, with the URL and the date it was read, or a written reason for the blank. Every one of these is PREVALENCE, never a dollar: none of the fee schedules we price from carries a sex field (the CMS physician fee schedule, the clinical laboratory fee schedule and the hospital outpatient file price a code, not a person), and no figure in this file is ever adjusted by sex. Where a federal file is silent, the blank says which file was read and where it stops, because a silence in the federal data is a finding about the data. data/verify_conditions.py re-reads every sex_note in its own source and fails if the source no longer says it.
